title: scheduled scale profiles + fairness-aware fleet scaler
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: customers with mixed workloads asked for predictable dedicated capacity behavior during known peak windows (daily batch jobs, nightly ingest, marketing campaigns) while preserving per-tenant fairness and soft throughput guarantees. This PR introduces a scheduler-based scale profile concept plus a fairness-aware scaler that reserves and enforces tenant headroom percentages during scheduled windows.

What this change does (high level): adds a ScaleProfile CRD-like config for Dedicated (stored in control plane tenant config), implements time-based scale profiles in the fleet autoscaler, and augments the scheduler to compute and enforce tenant headroom fractions. The scaler now supports: 1) scheduled up/down adjustments (scale profiles), 2) tenant-level soft guarantees (headroom_pct) that allocate reserved burst capacity, and 3) fairness rebalancing to avoid long-term capacity starvation.

Key behaviors and guarantees: - Scheduled profiles are applied with configurable pre-warm lead time (default 10m) to allow provisioning GPU pools before the window. - Headroom_pct is a soft-guarantee: the allocator attempts to preserve the specified percent of spare capacity per tenant but will yield if global capacity becomes constrained. - Fairness rebalancer runs every 60s and tries to minimize sustained deviation from baseline allocations; it is low-priority and will not preempt active requests.

Backward compatibility and migration: existing Dedicated configs continue to work. New config fields have defaults that preserve current autoscaler behavior (headroom_pct=0, no scheduled profiles). Migration plan: control plane database migration adds the scale_profiles table and backfills empty value; the fleet-controller tolerates both old and new records for 48 hours post-deploy.

Testing and telemetry: end-to-end integration tests added for scheduled windows, pre-warm behavior, and fairness under contention. New metrics: fleet_scale_profile_applied{profile,name}, tenant_headroom_utilization_pct, fairness_rebalance_actions_total. Dashboards updated: Dedicated -> Capacity -> Scheduled Profiles; an alert (SLO) for pre-warm misses added (dedicated.prewarm.miss > 0 for 5m).

Rollout plan: staged rollout: control plane first (feature flag), then fleet-controller + autoscaler; feature flag can be turned off to restore legacy behavior. We will enable for internal QA for 48h, then enable for a subset of enterprise tenants, and finally full rollout.

Checklist:
- [x] Autoscaler algorithm implemented and unit-tested
- [x] Scheduler integration + pre-warm hook
- [x] API surface for tenant scale profiles + schema migration
- [x] End-to-end tests for scheduled up/down and fairness rebalancing
- [x] Telemetry, dashboards, and alerting
- [x] Migration and rollback plan documented

Related items: Linear ENG-7321, ENG-7389; RFC: /docs/rfcs/fleet-schedule-profiles.md

Notes: there are a few known follow-ups tracked in ENG-7420 (deterministic allocation ordering) and ENG-7471 (adaptive pre-warm based on historical cold-starts).

review_comments: Marco Rivera (requested changes): The pre-warm lead time default of 10m seems conservative for small clusters; can we make it adaptive or expose cluster-level override?

Asha Patel (reply): Added cluster_override_ms config and plan to follow up with ENG-7471 for adaptive pre-warm based on historical cold-starts. Kept default 10m to be safe for customers we've seen miss capacity in tests.
Lina Chen (comment): DB migration looks sound but please ensure the migration is idempotent across control plane replicas.
Asha Patel (reply): Verified idempotency; migration uses IF NOT EXISTS and a lightweight backfill job with a lock. Added unit tests for migration run twice.
Priya Gupta (approved): Verified e2e test cases for fairness under contention. Metrics are meaningful and dashboards look good. Approving for merge after CI passes.

release_notes: Added scheduled scale profiles for Dedicated fleets and a fairness-aware fleet autoscaler. Operators can define time-based scale profiles to pre-warm capacity and set tenant headroom_pct to preserve burst capacity for important tenants. Metrics and dashboards added for observability. Feature is behind a control-plane feature flag and will be opt-in during rollout.
summary: Adds scheduled scaling profiles and a fairness-enabled autoscaler to improve predictability for scheduled workload peaks while preventing long-term tenant starvation. Includes API, migration, metrics, tests, and rollout plan.
